title: The Lost Homework
summary: A boy forgets his homework on the way to school and learns that staying calm, telling the truth, and making a real plan matter more than making an excuse.
poll: If you forget your homework, it is better to make a good excuse than to admit you forgot.

versions.title: The Lost Homework
versions.text:
Yusuf rides the bus to school.

One morning, he opens his bag to check his homework. It is not there! He left it on his desk at home.

Yusuf feels worried. He wants to panic. But he stops. He takes a breath.

Yusuf makes a plan. 'I will tell the truth,' he says. 'I will not make an excuse.'

At school, Yusuf walks to his teacher. Her name is Miss Nadia. He tells her the truth. 'I forgot my homework at home,' he says.

Miss Nadia asks, 'What is your plan?'

Yusuf says, 'I will bring it tomorrow. No excuse.'

Miss Nadia smiles. 'That is honest,' she says. 'I am proud of you.'

That night, Yusuf finishes his homework. He puts it by the door. Now he will not forget it again.

versions.title: The Lost Homework
versions.text:
Yusuf rides the yellow school bus to class every single morning, chatting happily with his friends along the bumpy ride through the quiet neighborhood streets near his home.

One ordinary morning, he opens his backpack to check his homework before the first bell rings, and his stomach drops immediately when he cannot find it. It is not there! He suddenly realizes, with a sinking feeling, that he left his notebook sitting on his desk at home, forgotten completely in the rush of the morning.

A wave of worry rushes through Yusuf's chest, and for a moment he feels like panicking completely and asking the bus driver to turn around. His hands turn cold and clammy, but he forces himself to stop moving and take a slow, deep breath instead of reacting without thinking.

Yusuf thinks carefully about what being responsible actually means in this difficult moment, rather than simply wishing the problem away. 'I will tell the truth,' he decides quietly to himself. 'I will not make up an excuse, even though a clever excuse might feel much easier to say right now.'

At school, Yusuf walks straight to his teacher before class begins, his heart beating fast with nervous energy the entire way there. Her name is Miss Nadia, and she is known around the school for being fair, patient, and genuinely understanding with her students. He admits the honest truth without hesitating for even a second. 'I forgot my homework at home,' he says simply.

Miss Nadia looks at him kindly and asks, 'What is your plan, and what do you think a fair consequence should be if this ever happens again?'

Yusuf answers clearly and thoughtfully, having already considered the question on his way to school. 'I will bring it tomorrow, finished completely, with no excuses at all. I will also build a new routine: I will put my finished homework by the front door every single night before I go to sleep, so I never forget it again.'

Miss Nadia smiles warmly at his thoughtful answer. 'I appreciate your honesty,' she says. 'Telling the truth and making a real, thoughtful plan matters far more to me than any clever excuse ever could, no matter how convincing.'

That night, Yusuf finishes all of his homework carefully and checks it twice before he feels satisfied. Then he places it right by the front door so he cannot possibly miss it in the morning rush. His new routine begins that very night, and he feels genuinely proud of himself instead of worried.

Yusuf's morning routine had become so familiar over the years that he barely noticed the bumpy ride on the yellow school bus anymore, chatting happily with his friends through the quiet neighborhood streets as the vehicle wound its way toward school.

One particular morning, as he opened his backpack to check his homework before the first bell rang, his stomach dropped immediately when his searching fingers failed to locate the notebook anywhere inside the crowded bag. It was not there; he realized, with a sinking feeling that spread through his entire body, that he had inadvertently left it sitting on his desk at home amid the hurried rush of getting ready.

A wave of worry rushed through Yusuf's chest, and for a moment he genuinely considered panicking and begging the bus driver to turn the vehicle around immediately. His hands turned cold and clammy, yet he forced himself to cease moving entirely and draw a slow, deliberate breath instead of reacting impulsively without carefully considering the situation first.

Yusuf reflected at length on what being responsible and accountable truly meant in such a genuinely difficult moment, rather than simply wishing that the problem would somehow resolve itself without any honesty or effort whatsoever on his part. 'I will tell the truth,' he decided quietly, his resolve strengthening with every passing second. Miss Nadia, who was known throughout the school for her fairness, patience, and genuine understanding toward every one of her students, listened as he admitted the honest truth without hesitating for even a moment, deliberately choosing honesty over comfort. 'I forgot my homework at home,' he said simply, meeting her eyes directly.

Miss Nadia regarded him thoughtfully and asked, 'What is your plan, and precisely how will you hold yourself accountable should something like this ever occur again?'

Yusuf answered clearly and thoughtfully, having already reflected carefully on the question throughout his ride to school that morning. I will also establish a new routine through sheer diligence, placing my finished homework directly beside the front door every single night before bed, so that forgetting it again becomes essentially impossible.'

questions.stem: What does Yusuf do that night so he will not forget his homework again?
options: He puts his homework by the front door
He asks his mother to carry his bag to school
He leaves his homework on the bus
He stops doing homework at home
questions.why: Yusuf finishes his homework and places it by the front door so he will see it in the morning.

wrong.B: The story does not say his mother carries his bag.
wrong.C: He does not leave his homework on the bus.
wrong.D: Yusuf keeps doing his homework; he just plans better.

questions.stem: What happens right after Yusuf tells Miss Nadia that he forgot his homework?
options: He rides the school bus all the way home
He puts his homework by the door
Miss Nadia asks him what his plan is
He finishes his homework
questions.why: After Yusuf admits he forgot his homework, Miss Nadia asks what his plan is.

wrong.A: Riding the bus home happens later, not right after.
wrong.B: Putting homework by the door happens that night, later in the story.
wrong.D: Finishing his homework happens that night, after talking to Miss Nadia.

LOW.prompt: Imagine you forgot something important for school, like Yusuf did. Write about what you would do. Use at least two ideas from the story.
checklist: I explained what I would do.
I used at least two ideas from the story.
I wrote complete sentences with capital letters and periods.
LOW.modelAnswer: If I forgot my homework like Yusuf, I would stay calm and take a deep breath instead of panicking. Then I would tell my teacher the honest truth instead of making an excuse. I would also make a plan, like bringing it the next day with no excuses. Being honest would make me feel proud, just like Yusuf.

keyWords.definition: able to be trusted to do the right thing
keyWords.example: A responsible student remembers to bring their books to class.

keyWords.definition: to say that something is true, especially something you did wrong
keyWords.example: He had to admit that he broke the window.

keyWords.definition: a result that happens because of something you did
keyWords.example: Staying up too late can have a consequence the next morning.

keyWords.definition: a regular habit done the same way again and again
keyWords.example: Brushing your teeth every night is part of a good routine.

keyWords.definition: to be thankful for something or recognize its value
keyWords.example: I appreciate it when my friends tell me the truth.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states what this story is mainly about?
options: Yusuf forgets his homework and chooses honesty and a real plan over an excuse
Yusuf decides that homework assignments do not matter very much
Yusuf's teacher cancels homework for the rest of the entire class
Yusuf's friend lends him an already finished homework notebook
questions.why: The story follows Yusuf as he forgets his homework and chooses to be honest and make a real plan rather than make an excuse.

wrong.B: Yusuf keeps caring about his homework; he does not decide it is unimportant.
wrong.C: The teacher does not cancel homework in the story.
wrong.D: No friend lends Yusuf a notebook in the story.

questions.stem: What does Yusuf realize just as the bus is on its way to school?
options: He left his homework notebook on his desk at home
He forgot to pack his lunch that morning
He missed his usual bus stop by one block
He forgot his pencil case at his cousin's house
questions.why: Yusuf realizes on the bus that he left his homework notebook on his desk at home.

wrong.B: The story does not mention lunch.
wrong.C: The story does not say he missed a bus stop.
wrong.D: The story does not mention a pencil case.

questions.stem: What question does Miss Nadia ask Yusuf after he admits he forgot his homework?
options: Why didn't you ask a friend for help?
Who else in your family knows about this problem?
What is your plan if this happens again?
Why did you not bring an excuse note?
questions.why: Miss Nadia asks Yusuf about his plan and what a fair consequence should be.

wrong.A: Miss Nadia does not ask about a friend.
wrong.B: Miss Nadia does not ask who else knows.
wrong.D: Miss Nadia does not ask about an excuse note.

questions.stem: In the story, the word routine most nearly means —
options: a single excuse that a student uses only one time
a strict punishment given by a teacher
a surprise plan made at the last moment
a regular habit done the same way again and again
questions.why: Yusuf's new routine is putting his finished homework by the door every single night, a regular habit.

wrong.A: A routine is not a single excuse.
wrong.B: A routine is not a punishment.
wrong.C: A routine is repeated, not a one-time surprise.

questions.stem: Why does Yusuf choose to admit the truth instead of making an excuse, even though an excuse might feel easier?
options: He believes honesty matters more than comfort
He is afraid Miss Nadia will find out anyway
He cannot think of any good excuse to use
His friends tell him he should confess the truth
questions.why: Yusuf decides on his own that honesty and responsibility matter more than the comfort of an easy excuse.

wrong.B: The story does not say he is afraid of being caught.
wrong.C: The story does not say he cannot think of an excuse.
wrong.D: The story does not mention his friends telling him anything.

questions.stem: Compare how Yusuf feels right after discovering his homework is missing with how he feels after making his plan with Miss Nadia.
options: He feels proud at first, then embarrassed afterward
He feels angry at first, then quite bored afterward about it
He feels worried at first, then calm after making a plan
He feels calm the whole time and never worries at all
questions.why: Yusuf first feels worried when he discovers his homework is missing, but he feels proud and calm after making a real plan with Miss Nadia.

wrong.A: The story never describes pride turning to embarrassment.
wrong.B: The story never describes anger or boredom.
wrong.D: The story clearly describes worry, not constant calm.

questions.stem: Why does Yusuf decide to put his finished homework by the front door every night?
options: Miss Nadia told him he must do it or be punished
He wants to build a routine so he will not forget again
His parents ask him to clean up the house
He has no extra room left inside his backpack today
questions.why: Yusuf builds this new routine on his own so that he will not forget his homework again.

wrong.A: Miss Nadia does not force him to do this.
wrong.C: The story does not mention cleaning the house.
wrong.D: The story does not mention a lack of room.

questions.stem: Put these events in order: Yusuf admits he forgot his homework; Yusuf notices his homework is missing; Miss Nadia appreciates his honesty; Yusuf makes a plan for a new routine.
options: admits, notices missing, appreciates, makes plan
appreciates, makes plan, notices missing, admits
notices missing, makes plan, admits, appreciates
notices missing, admits, makes plan, appreciates
questions.why: Yusuf first notices his homework is missing, then admits it to Miss Nadia, then makes a plan for a new routine, and Miss Nadia appreciates his honesty.

wrong.A: This places noticing after admitting, which is backwards.
wrong.B: This places appreciating before anything has even happened.
wrong.C: This places making the plan before Yusuf has admitted anything.

MID.prompt: Explain how Yusuf shows responsibility after he realizes he forgot his homework. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained how Yusuf shows responsibility.
I used at least two details from the story.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: Yusuf shows responsibility by staying calm instead of panicking when he discovers his homework is missing. He admits the truth to Miss Nadia instead of making an excuse, and he also makes a real plan: he will bring the homework finished tomorrow and build a new routine of placing it by the door each night. Miss Nadia appreciates his honesty because it shows he is taking responsibility for his mistake.

keyWords.definition: the quality of doing the right thing, even when no one is watching
keyWords.example: A person with integrity returns money they find, even if no one would know.

keyWords.definition: responsible for your own actions and ready to answer for them
keyWords.example: A good leader stays accountable when a plan does not work out.

keyWords.definition: done on purpose, after careful thought
keyWords.example: She made a deliberate choice to study instead of watching television.

keyWords.definition: to think carefully about something, often about your own actions
keyWords.example: After the test, she took time to reflect on what she could improve.

keyWords.definition: careful and steady effort put into a task
keyWords.example: His diligence in practicing every day helped him improve quickly.

questions.stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of this story?
options: A boy forgets his homework and shows integrity by choosing honesty over an excuse
A teacher punishes a boy severely for forgetting his homework
A boy avoids all consequences by crafting a clever and convincing excuse
A boy decides that daily routines are unnecessary once he turns in late work
questions.why: The story centers on Yusuf's integrity: he chooses honesty and a deliberate plan rather than an excuse after forgetting his homework.

wrong.B: Miss Nadia does not punish him severely; she praises his honesty.
wrong.C: Yusuf does not avoid consequences with an excuse; he admits the truth.
wrong.D: Yusuf builds a routine rather than deciding routines are unnecessary.

questions.stem: In the story, integrity most nearly means —
options: the habit of making convincing excuses
doing right even when no one is watching
a strict schedule used only for homework time
a feeling of fear before speaking to a teacher
questions.why: Yusuf says integrity means doing the right thing even when nobody is watching, choosing truth over an easier excuse.

wrong.A: Integrity is the opposite of making excuses.
wrong.C: A schedule is a routine, not integrity.
wrong.D: Integrity is about honesty, not fear.

questions.stem: What specific step does Yusuf commit to as part of holding himself accountable?
options: Asking a friend to remind him about homework every morning
Asking Miss Nadia to call his parents
Placing finished homework by the door every night
Skipping homework until he feels ready
questions.why: Yusuf commits to a new routine of placing his finished homework by the front door every single night.

wrong.A: The story does not mention a friend reminding him.
wrong.B: The story does not mention calling his parents.
wrong.D: Yusuf plans to keep doing his homework, not skip it.

questions.stem: What does Yusuf's immediate decision to tell the truth, rather than invent an excuse, suggest about his character?
options: He is afraid of being caught in a lie later
He does not understand that excuses are an option
He wants Miss Nadia to feel genuinely sorry for him today
He values honesty even when it would be easier to lie
questions.why: Yusuf chooses the harder, honest path even though an excuse would have been easier, showing that he values honesty.

wrong.A: The story presents this as a choice of integrity, not fear of being caught.
wrong.B: Yusuf clearly considers and rejects the idea of an excuse.
wrong.C: The story gives no indication he wants sympathy.

questions.stem: Compare Yusuf's state of mind right after discovering his homework missing with his state of mind after he reflects and commits to a plan.
options: He moves from anxious panic to a steady, deliberate resolve
He remains equally anxious throughout both moments
He feels proud at first, and ashamed afterward
He feels bored at first, and alarmed afterward
questions.why: Yusuf first feels a wave of worry and the urge to panic, but after reflecting he grows steadier and more resolved.

wrong.B: His anxiety clearly lessens once he commits to a plan.
wrong.C: The story never describes pride turning to shame.
wrong.D: The story never describes boredom at the start.

questions.stem: Why does Miss Nadia value Yusuf's honest admission more than a clever excuse would have been?
options: Because excuses are against the school's official rules
Because an honest, deliberate plan shows real accountability
Because Yusuf is the only student who ever forgets homework
Because Miss Nadia almost always dislikes hearing any such explanations
questions.why: Miss Nadia says telling the truth and making a real, deliberate plan matters far more to her than any clever excuse.

wrong.A: The story never mentions a school rule against excuses.
wrong.C: The story does not say Yusuf is the only student to forget homework.
wrong.D: The story never says Miss Nadia dislikes explanations in general.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly matches the order of events in the story?
options: Yusuf builds a new routine; he notices his homework is missing; he reflects on integrity; he admits the truth
Yusuf admits the truth; he notices his homework is missing; he builds a new routine; he reflects on integrity
Yusuf notices his homework is missing; he reflects on integrity; he admits the truth; he builds a new routine
Yusuf reflects on integrity; he builds a new routine; he notices his homework is missing; he admits the truth
questions.why: Yusuf first notices his homework is missing, reflects on integrity, admits the truth to Miss Nadia, and finally builds a new routine.

wrong.A: This places building the routine before he even notices the homework is missing.
wrong.B: This places admitting the truth before he notices the problem.
wrong.D: This places reflecting and building the routine before he notices anything is wrong.

questions.stem: Why does the author most likely include Miss Nadia's question about accountability?
options: To show that Miss Nadia is only ever interested in punishing mistakes
To suggest that homework assignments do not really matter very much at all
To explain in detail how school rules about late work are formally written
To highlight that real responsibility includes a concrete plan, not just an apology
questions.why: Miss Nadia's question pushes Yusuf to form a concrete plan, showing that true responsibility is more than simply saying sorry.

wrong.A: Miss Nadia praises Yusuf rather than punishing him.
wrong.B: The story treats homework as important, not unimportant.
wrong.C: The story never explains formal school rules about late work.

HIGH.prompt: Some people think admitting a mistake is a sign of weakness, while others think it shows integrity. Which do you agree with? Support your answer with evidence from the story.
checklist: I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed a point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that admitting a mistake shows integrity rather than weakness. Yusuf could have invented an excuse when he realized he forgot his homework, but instead he chose honesty, even though it was uncomfortable. His deliberate plan, including building a diligent new routine, shows real accountability rather than avoidance. Someone might argue that a good excuse would have been simpler, but Miss Nadia's reaction shows that honesty earned Yusuf more trust than any clever excuse could have.
